CoraFull was sensitive to the ball budget: reducing Bmax from 64 to 32 lowered mean accuracy by 2.10 percentage points, whereas increasing it to 128 improved accuracy by 1.57 points. old: GB-LCSS uses labels from related training nodes to supplement an individual annotation. When most of these nodes provide evidence for the current node's underlying class, aggregating their labels can reduce the influence of an isolated annotation error. Label-free grouping prevents corrupted annotations from determining which nodes provide this evidence, while excluding the current node prevents its own label from reinforcing the consensus used to adjust it. The comparisons with random size-matched grouping and generic smoothing (Table 5), together with the lower target Brier scores (Fig. 4), support the importance of selecting informative local evidence rather than simply softening the targets.
new: GB-LCSS supplements an individual annotation with labels from related training nodes. Label-free grouping keeps corrupted annotations from shaping the groups, while excluding the current node prevents its label from reinforcing the consensus used to adjust it. Proposition 1 quantifies the reliability of the local vote when the true class is more frequent than any competing class among the voting nodes and labels are corrupted independently by symmetric noise. The random-grouping and smoothing controls (Table 5) support the value of selecting informative local evidence. The target-error decomposition in Appendix I.2 further shows how the targets improved: the reduction in error on corrupted labels outweighed the increase on initially correct labels in the tested runs.

old: Granular balls organize local-consensus supervision into shared regions. Each node is assigned to exactly one group, and the resulting class statistics can be reused across the targets constructed within that group. The prescribed budget also bounds the number of regions to be maintained. In Table 6, granular ball grouping achieves accuracy within one percentage point of both kNN and k-means on four of the five datasets; on CoraFull, kNN is higher by 3.11 points. Granular ball grouping also uses less storage than exact kNN on the three larger datasets and has the shortest construction time on three of the five datasets in the reported measurements (Fig. 5). These results support granular balls as a practical choice for combining competitive accuracy with shared regional statistics and favorable grouping costs.
new: Granular balls organize this supervision into shared regions. Each node is assigned to one group, class statistics are reused within that group, and the prescribed budget bounds the number of regions. The sensitivity results in Section 4.3.4 show why local grouping and voting coverage matter: the largest losses occurred when all nodes remained in one ball or substantially fewer nodes received consensus supervision. In Table 6, granular ball grouping achieves accuracy within one percentage point of both kNN and k-means on four of the five datasets; on CoraFull, kNN is higher by 3.11 points. Granular ball grouping also uses less storage than exact kNN on the three larger datasets and has the shortest construction time on three of the five datasets in the reported measurements (Fig. 5). Together, these results support granular balls as a practical choice for combining competitive accuracy with shared regional statistics and favorable grouping costs.

old: We also examined the local-class condition in Proposition 1. Using clean labels for this diagnostic, we counted training nodes whose true class had more votes than any other class among the other training nodes in their ball. Averaged over seeds, these fractions were 75.64%, 65.02%, and 36.13% on Cora, CiteSeer, and CoraFull, respectively. The condition is node-specific: a dominant class within a ball can provide useful evidence for members of that class while disagreeing with other members.
